name: George Washington
accomplishments: Set the precedent of a two-term presidency
Established the first Cabinet
Issued the Neutrality Proclamation (1793)
Suppressed the Whiskey Rebellion (1794)
Farewell Address warned against permanent foreign alliances and political factions

name: John Adams

positions.label: Lawyer; defended British soldiers after the Boston Massacre
Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Avoided full-scale war with France during the Quasi-War
Signed (and later regretted) the Alien and Sedition Acts (1798)
Built up the U.S. Navy
Peacefully ceded power after losing re-election in 1800

name: Thomas Jefferson

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

career: Principal author of the Declaration of Independence (1776)
Founder of the University of Virginia
accomplishments: Louisiana Purchase (1803) doubled the size of the U.S.
Commissioned the Lewis and Clark Expedition
Signed the Embargo Act (1807)

name: James Madison
career: Chief drafter of the U.S. Constitution — "Father of the Constitution"
accomplishments: Led the U.S. through the War of 1812
White House burned by British forces (1814)
Signed the charter of the Second Bank of the United States (1816)

name: James Monroe
accomplishments: Monroe Doctrine (1823) opposed European colonization in the Americas
Missouri Compromise (1820) signed into law
Acquired Florida from Spain (1819)
Presided over the "Era of Good Feelings"

name: John Quincy Adams

positions.label: Minister to the Netherlands, Prussia, Russia & Britain

accomplishments: Pushed federally funded roads, canals, and a national university
Argued the Amistad case before the Supreme Court (1841), post-presidency
Collapsed and died on the floor of the House (1848)

name: Andrew Jackson

positions.label: Major General; Battle of New Orleans (War of 1812)

accomplishments: Signed the Indian Removal Act (1830), leading to the Trail of Tears
Vetoed re-charter of the Second Bank of the United States
Faced down the Nullification Crisis with South Carolina (1832–33)

name: Martin Van Buren

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Presidency dominated by the Panic of 1837
Established an independent U.S. Treasury
Avoided war with Britain over the Canadian border

name: William Henry Harrison

positions.label: Army officer; Battle of Tippecanoe & War of 1812

accomplishments: Delivered the longest inaugural address in history, then died of illness 31 days later — the shortest presidency on record

name: John Tyler

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: First VP to succeed a president who died in office, establishing the succession precedent ("Tyler Precedent")
Annexation of Texas (1845)
Expelled from the Whig Party while in office

name: James K. Polk
accomplishments: Mexican-American War (1846–48) added vast Southwest territory
Settled the Oregon boundary dispute with Britain at the 49th parallel
Did not seek re-election, as promised; died three months after leaving office

name: Zachary Taylor

positions.label: U.S. Army career, incl. Mexican-American War command

accomplishments: Opposed the spread of slavery into new territories
Died in office of an acute illness after 16 months

name: Millard Fillmore

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Signed the Compromise of 1850, delaying sectional crisis over slavery
Sent Commodore Perry to open trade with Japan (1852)

name: Franklin Pierce
accomplishments: Signed the Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854), deepening sectional conflict over slavery
Gadsden Purchase (1853) added land to the Southwest

name: James Buchanan
accomplishments: Presided over the country's fracture in the run-up to the Civil War
Dred Scott decision handed down days into his term (1857)
Left office as seven states had already seceded

name: Abraham Lincoln
career: Famed 1858 Senate debates with Stephen Douglas
accomplishments: Preserved the Union through the Civil War (1861–65)
Emancipation Proclamation (1863)
Gettysburg Address (1863)
Signed the 13th Amendment abolishing slavery
Assassinated by John Wilkes Booth days after Confederate surrender

name: Andrew Johnson

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Oversaw early Reconstruction after Lincoln's assassination
First president impeached by the House (1868); acquitted by one Senate vote
Clashed repeatedly with the Radical Republican Congress

name: Ulysses S. Grant

positions.label: Farmer, then leather-goods clerk (repeated business failures)
Union Army, Civil War; Commanding General

accomplishments: Worked to enforce Reconstruction and civil rights in the South
Signed the Enforcement Acts against the Ku Klux Klan
Administration troubled by financial scandals (e.g., Crédit Mobilier, Whiskey Ring)

name: Rutherford B. Hayes

positions.label: Union Army officer, wounded in action

accomplishments: Won a bitterly disputed 1876 election settled by the Compromise of 1877
Ended Reconstruction by withdrawing federal troops from the South
Pledged (and kept his pledge) to serve only one term

name: James A. Garfield

positions.label: Teacher, then president of Hiram College (Eclectic Institute)

accomplishments: Shot by a disgruntled office-seeker four months into office; lingered 79 days before dying
Death spurred civil-service reform (Pendleton Act, 1883)

name: Chester A. Arthur

positions.label: Quartermaster General, New York Militia (Civil War, non-combat)
Collector of the Port of New York
Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Signed the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act (1883)
Modernized the U.S. Navy
Signed the Chinese Exclusion Act (1882)

name: Grover Cleveland
accomplishments: Only president to serve two non-consecutive terms
Vetoed hundreds of private pension bills he viewed as fraudulent
Second term dominated by the Panic of 1893
Secretly had cancer surgery aboard a yacht (1893) to hide it from the public

name: Benjamin Harrison
career: Grandson of President William Henry Harrison
accomplishments: Signed the Sherman Antitrust Act (1890)
Admitted six new states to the Union
Sherman Silver Purchase Act (1890)

name: William McKinley
accomplishments: Led the U.S. to victory in the Spanish-American War (1898)
Acquired the Philippines, Puerto Rico, and Guam
Assassinated by an anarchist at the Pan-American Exposition, Buffalo

name: Theodore Roosevelt

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Trust-busting under the Sherman Antitrust Act
Built the Panama Canal
Vast expansion of national parks and forests
Negotiated the end of the Russo-Japanese War — Nobel Peace Prize (1906)
Youngest president ever, at 42

name: William Howard Taft

positions.label: Chief Justice of the United States

accomplishments: Continued antitrust enforcement, including breakup of Standard Oil (1911)
16th Amendment (federal income tax) proposed under his term
Only person to serve as both President and Chief Justice

name: Woodrow Wilson

positions.label: Lawyer, then professor of political science

accomplishments: Created the Federal Reserve System (1913)
Led the U.S. through World War I
Proposed the League of Nations; Nobel Peace Prize (1919)
Suffered a debilitating stroke in office (1919), largely concealed from the public

name: Warren G. Harding
accomplishments: Presided over a postwar economic boom ("Return to Normalcy")
Administration later marred by the Teapot Dome scandal, exposed after his death
Died suddenly of a heart attack while traveling in San Francisco

name: Calvin Coolidge

positions.label: Massachusetts state legislature & Mayor of Northampton
Vice President of the United States

career: Broke the Boston police strike as governor (1919)
accomplishments: Presided over the Roaring Twenties economic boom
Cut federal taxes and spending

name: Herbert Hoover

positions.label: Head of Belgian & European war relief efforts

career: Later led relief commissions for Truman and Eisenhower
accomplishments: Stock market crashed seven months into his term (Oct. 1929)
Response to the Great Depression widely seen as inadequate

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
career: Contracted polio in 1921, largely paralyzed from the waist down
accomplishments: The New Deal (1933–39) reshaped the federal government's role in the economy
Led the Allies through most of World War II
Only president elected to four terms (led to the 22nd Amendment)
Died in office weeks before Germany's surrender

name: Harry S. Truman

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Ordered the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, ending WWII
Launched the Marshall Plan and the Truman Doctrine (Cold War containment)
Recognized the State of Israel (1948)
Led the U.S. into the Korean War
Desegregated the U.S. armed forces (1948)

name: Dwight D. Eisenhower

positions.label: U.S. Army career; Supreme Allied Commander, Europe (WWII)

accomplishments: Oversaw D-Day and Allied victory in Europe as wartime commander
Ended the Korean War
Built the Interstate Highway System (1956)
Sent federal troops to enforce school desegregation in Little Rock (1957)
Warned of the "military-industrial complex" in his farewell address

name: John F. Kennedy
accomplishments: Navigated the Cuban Missile Crisis (1962)
Launched the Apollo program's goal of landing on the Moon
Established the Peace Corps
Assassinated in Dallas, Texas — youngest elected president to die in office

name: Lyndon B. Johnson

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Civil Rights Act (1964) and Voting Rights Act (1965)
Great Society programs — Medicare, Medicaid, War on Poverty
Dramatically escalated U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War
Chose not to seek re-election in 1968 amid war unrest

name: Richard Nixon

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Opened diplomatic relations with China (1972)
Ended U.S. combat involvement in Vietnam
Established the EPA (1970)
Only president to resign, over the Watergate scandal

name: Gerald Ford

positions.label: Assistant football coach, Yale; lawyer, Michigan
U.S. House of Representatives (MI), Minority Leader

accomplishments: Only president never elected as president or vice president
Pardoned Nixon a month into office, a deeply controversial decision
Signed the Helsinki Accords (1975)

name: Jimmy Carter

positions.label: Post-presidency: Carter Center & Habitat for Humanity

accomplishments: Brokered the Camp David Accords between Egypt and Israel (1978)
Iran Hostage Crisis dominated his final 444 days in office
Established the Departments of Energy and Education
Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize (2002) for post-presidency work

name: Ronald Reagan

positions.label: Army Air Forces, First Motion Picture Unit (WWII)
Hollywood actor; President of the Screen Actors Guild

accomplishments: Survived an assassination attempt 69 days into office (1981)
Major tax cuts and deregulation ("Reaganomics")
Escalated the arms race, then signed the INF Treaty with Gorbachev (1987)
Called for the Berlin Wall to be torn down (1987), which fell in 1989

name: George H. W. Bush

positions.label: Navy pilot, shot down in combat (WWII)
Oil businessman, co-founder of Zapata Petroleum
Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Led the Gulf War coalition against Iraq (1991)
Presided over the peaceful end of the Cold War and Soviet collapse
Signed the Americans with Disabilities Act (1990)

name: Bill Clinton
accomplishments: Signed NAFTA (1994)
Balanced the federal budget, produced a budget surplus
Welfare reform (1996)
Impeached by the House over the Lewinsky scandal (1998); acquitted by the Senate

name: George W. Bush

positions.label: Managing partner, Texas Rangers baseball team

accomplishments: Led the response to the September 11, 2001 attacks
Launched the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq
No Child Left Behind Act (2001)
Managed the federal response to the 2008 financial crisis (TARP)

name: Barack Obama
accomplishments: Affordable Care Act (2010)
Presided over recovery from the 2008 financial crisis
Ordered the operation that killed Osama bin Laden (2011)
Normalized relations with Cuba; joined the Paris Climate Agreement
First African American president

name: Donald Trump
career: First president with no prior military or government experience before taking office
accomplishments: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2017)
Appointed three Supreme Court justices in his first term
Brokered the Abraham Accords (2020)
Impeached twice by the House (2019, 2021); acquitted both times by the Senate
Second, non-consecutive term began January 20, 2025 — the second president to do so after Grover Cleveland

name: Joe Biden

positions.label: Vice President of the United States

accomplishments: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021)
CHIPS and Science Act (2022)
Oversaw the withdrawal of U.S. forces from Afghanistan (2021)
Oldest person inaugurated as president
